Central Football Club, commonly known as Central or CFC, is a professional football club based in Bute Town, Wajir North Sub-County, Kenya. They compete in the local football league in Bute Town. Central FC are among the four founding football clubs in Bute along Al-Ahly FC, Dokono FC and Simba FC. Domestically they have won one title in 2022.

History

Formation and early years

Central Football Club was established in 2012 in Bute Town. During its early period, the club was among the first group of football clubs associated with the development of organised football in the town.

The club's first generation was built around a group of young and talented players. Jimcale served as the club's first coach.

Central enjoyed a successful beginning and attracted attention for the quality of its young players. Several of the team's standout players subsequently moved to other clubs. Abdikadir “Jones” remained associated with Central and later became an important link between the club's original generation and its subsequent revival.

Following the departure of much of its original playing group, Central became inactive for approximately one year.

Revival

Central Football Club was revived in 2013, beginning a new chapter in its history.

During the revival period, the club initially operated without a permanent coach. Mohamed Omar played an important role during this period as the club rebuilt its playing group and returned to competitive football.

The revival generation included several players who became associated with the club's early modern history:

  • Cade — first captain following the 2013 revival
  • Rashka — defensive midfielder known for his tackling
  • Aley J — later became the club's longest-serving captain
  • Abdikadir “Jones” — the only player to remain from the first generation

This generation helped re-establish Central's identity and competitive presence in Bute Town.

Matches against teams from outside Bute

One notable aspect of Central's early history was its participation in matches against teams from outside Bute Town.

The club's first recorded match against an opponent from outside Bute was against Funanbua FC of Buna in 2015.

Funanbua 0–1 Central · 2015
Central won the match 1–0, with Major Yahya scoring the winning goal. The match is particularly remembered in the club's history because Central travelled with only 11 players, leaving the team without substitutes.

2022 Hon. GK Tournament

One of the defining moments in Central Football Club's history came in 2022, when the club reached the final of the Hon. GK Tournament.

Quarter-final: Central vs Gumar

Central were drawn against Gumar FC in the quarter-final. The match ended 0-0 after normal play. With neither side able to break the deadlock, the tie proceeded to a penalty shootout.

Central prevailed on penalties to advance to the semi-final.

Gumar vs Central
Match during Hon GK
Tournament in 2022

Semi-final: Central vs Homeboys

Central faced Homeboys in the semi-final.

The match produced a memorable moment when Buffon, a former Central defender, scored for Homeboys with a powerful long-range strike from around the halfway line.

Central continued to push for an equaliser as the match approached its conclusion. Late in the game Mohaa scored an own goal bringing the score 1-1.

The match subsequently went to a penalty shootout. Central held their nerve and won the shootout, securing their place in the tournament final.

Final: Central vs Al Ahly

In the final Central faced an in-form Al Ahly side that had impressed during the tournament after recording heavy victories over Simba FC and Dokono FC.

Central remained disciplined throughout the final and managed to keep Al Ahly from scoring.

The match ended 0-0 after normal play.

Once again the tournament was decided by penalties. Central won the penalty shootout to become the 2022 Hon. GK Tournament Champions.

Central players celebrating their trophy
Win over Al Ahly in 2022

2024 season

Central reached two major tournament finals during 2024.

Abdiaziz Gardale BBC Tournament

Central reached the final of the Abdiaziz Gardale BBC Tournament and finished as runners-up, losing the final 0-1 to Simba FC.

Mwalimu Abdinoor SCDE Tournament

Central also reached the final of the Mwalimu Abdinoor SCDE Tournament and finished as runners-up, losing the final 0–2 to Al Ahly FC.

Before reaching the final, Central defeated Dokono FC 1–0 in the semi-final.

Club captains

Captaincy has formed an important part of Central Football Club's history.

Cade became the first captain following the club's 2013 revival.

Aley J subsequently became the club's longest-serving captain.

The current captain is Abdullahi Yussuf, with Abdirizack Mohamed serving as assistant captain.

Playing identity

Central Football Club's traditional visual identity is based around navy blue, red and gold.

The nickname “The Walls” is associated with the club's defensive tradition and its historical reputation for defensive organisation and strong defensive players.

Club culture and legacy

Central Football Club's history is closely connected to the development of football in Bute Town.

The club's identity has developed through several generations of players, coaches and officials. Its early years were characterised by young players, competitive local matches and a strong emphasis on defensive organisation.

The nickname “The Walls” became associated with this defensive identity and remains part of the club's character.

The 2022 Hon. GK Tournament victory represents a significant milestone in the club's recorded history. Central's appearances in major tournament finals in 2024 subsequently added another chapter to its competitive record.

The club's historical archive continues to develop through photographs, match records, tournament materials, player histories and accounts from former players and officials.

Current Generation

Current club management

Mr Abdirizack Billow who recently joined the club serves as the chairman of the board of directors of Central FC. Assisted by him are club CEO Mr Ahmed Abdi and club patron Mr Abdijabar Ali who was recently promoted to patron following the clubs changes made in the hierarchy. Mohamed Ali is the current head coach assisted by former captain Aley J and Sitar Mohamed.
